answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each identity expensive to mint and cheap to verify: a new agent must burn a small fee and complete a verifiable-delay computation before it receives its onyx identity token, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand burns and delays. Honest agents pay once and then build an opal record of completed jobs, while a plume of fresh, history-free identities is rate-limited to low-value tasks until it earns trust through attested work. That asymmetry, linear for attackers and one-time for honest agents, keeps the registry honest.
